pedagogicalDesign.title: First-Principles Narrative + Pragmatic Craftsmanship
pedagogicalDesign.description: Every static lesson opens with a failure-first story ('why this exists'), lets learners toggle three static explanation lenses (Intuition, Production Mechanics, Staff Trade-Offs), embeds pause-and-predict Socratic prompts before critical failures, and grounds decisions in DDIA chapters and Pragmatic Programmer heuristics.

ddiaChapterMap.title: Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Applications
coreMentalModels: Faults vs Failures: anticipate hardware, software, and human faults before they cascade into outages
Describe load using explicit parameters (fan-out, read/write ratio) and measure tail latency (p95, p99, p999) rather than misleading averages
Operability, simplicity, and evolvability determine long-term velocity

ddiaChapterMap.title: Data Models and Query Languages
coreMentalModels: Relational joins shine for many-to-many data; Document models shine for self-contained trees with locality
Impedance mismatch and schema-on-read vs schema-on-write
Declarative queries let engines optimize execution plans under the hood

ddiaChapterMap.title: Storage and Retrieval
coreMentalModels: LSM-Trees (MemTable + WAL + SSTable compaction) optimize sequential writes at the cost of read/compaction amplification
B-Trees optimize in-place page reads/updates with predictable latency and simpler transactional locks
OLTP row stores vs OLAP column-oriented compressed storage

ddiaChapterMap.title: Encoding and Evolution
coreMentalModels: Binary schema evolution (Protobuf, Thrift, Avro) via field tags preserves backward and forward compatibility during rolling deploys
Data flows across databases, REST/gRPC RPCs, and async event brokers

ddiaChapterMap.title: Replication
coreMentalModels: Single-leader replication lag causes read-your-writes, monotonic-read, and consistent-prefix anomalies
Multi-leader replication introduces concurrent write conflicts (LWW vs CRDTs)
Leaderless Dynamo quorums (W + R > N), sloppy quorums, and vector-clock causality

ddiaChapterMap.title: Partitioning
coreMentalModels: Key-range partitioning preserves range scans but risks hot-spot skew; Hash/Consistent-Hash partitioning spreads load evenly
Secondary indexes (local document-partitioned scatter-gather vs global term-partitioned)
Fixed logical partitions/vnodes keep rebalancing safe

ddiaChapterMap.title: Transactions
coreMentalModels: Weak isolation stops dirty reads/writes, yet Snapshot Isolation still suffers Write Skew and Phantom Reads
True Serializability comes via single-threaded execution, 2PL, or optimistic Serializable Snapshot Isolation (SSI)

ddiaChapterMap.title: The Trouble with Distributed Systems
coreMentalModels: Unbounded network delays, asymmetric partitions, and stop-the-world GC pauses break wall-clock timeouts
Time-of-day NTP clocks can jump backward—never rely on wall clocks for ordering or lease safety
Monotonic fencing tokens protect resources when a paused lock holder wakes up late

ddiaChapterMap.title: Consistency and Consensus
coreMentalModels: Linearizability (recency guarantee on a single register) vs Serializability (multi-object transaction isolation)
CAP/PACELC: partitions force choosing consistency or availability; normal operation forces latency vs consistency
Raft/Paxos consensus turns total-order broadcast and ZooKeeper/etcd coordination into safe primitives

ddiaChapterMap.title: Batch Processing
coreMentalModels: Immutable inputs + deterministic transformations enable safe retries and clean reprocessing
Sort-merge / map-side joins and dataflow engines separate compute from durable state

ddiaChapterMap.title: Stream Processing
coreMentalModels: Append-only partitioned logs (Kafka) turn databases into streams via Change Data Capture (CDC) & Outbox
Event time vs processing time, watermarking, and idempotent sinks for effective-once semantics

ddiaChapterMap.title: The Future of Data Systems
coreMentalModels: Unbundling databases: derive caches, search indexes, and vector stores reliably from an immutable event log
End-to-end auditability, idempotent request IDs, and correctness verification across heterogeneous stores

pragmaticPrinciples.name: ETC (Easier To Change)
pragmaticPrinciples.coreIdea: Every architectural choice—coupling, data format, service boundary—is judged by whether it makes tomorrow's requirement change easier or harder.
pragmaticPrinciples.hldApplication: Keep schemas backward-compatible, decouple async side-effects behind event logs, and avoid leaky database assumptions in public APIs.
pragmaticPrinciples.lldApplication: Program to interfaces/abstractions and invert dependencies so implementations swap cleanly.

pragmaticPrinciples.name: Orthogonality (Eliminate Hidden Coupling)
pragmaticPrinciples.coreIdea: Changing one component should not ripple unexpectedly into unrelated subsystems.
pragmaticPrinciples.hldApplication: Isolate rate limiting, auth, caching, and business compute behind clean gateway/service seams; shard by tenant/city so Mumbai traffic never destabilizes London.
pragmaticPrinciples.lldApplication: Single Responsibility Principle, clean modules, and pure unit-testable domain logic.

pragmaticPrinciples.name: Reversibility (No Final Decisions)
pragmaticPrinciples.coreIdea: Treat database engines, cloud vendors, and model providers as replaceable adapters written in sand—not stone.
pragmaticPrinciples.hldApplication: Hide storage behind domain APIs, use standard HTTP/gRPC/S3 protocols, and design model-routing gateways so SLMs and frontier LLMs swap effortlessly.
pragmaticPrinciples.lldApplication: Repository, Adapter, and Strategy patterns isolating volatile third-party SDKs.

pragmaticPrinciples.name: Tracer Bullets (End-to-End Thin Slices)
pragmaticPrinciples.coreIdea: Ship a minimal connected path from client to storage and back early so real latency, bottlenecks, and integration seams surface immediately.
pragmaticPrinciples.hldApplication: Walk interviews and prototypes end-to-end (Client -> Gateway -> Service -> DB -> Response) before prematurely optimizing exotic edge tiers.
pragmaticPrinciples.lldApplication: Build one working vertical feature with tests before expanding abstractions.

pragmaticPrinciples.name: DRY (Single Authoritative Source of Truth)
pragmaticPrinciples.coreIdea: Every piece of knowledge or state must have one unambiguous owner; derived caches and search indexes are projections, never competing truths.
pragmaticPrinciples.hldApplication: Never dual-write directly from app code to Postgres + Redis/Elasticsearch without Outbox/CDC or cache invalidation rules—derive projections from the single system of record.
pragmaticPrinciples.lldApplication: Avoid duplicated business invariants across validators, UI, and handlers.

pragmaticPrinciples.name: Crash Early & Dead Programs Tell No Lies
pragmaticPrinciples.coreIdea: Silently swallowing corruption or hanging indefinitely causes cascading exhaustion; fail fast with bounded timeouts, circuit breakers, and DLQs.
pragmaticPrinciples.hldApplication: Enforce strict deadlines, reject malformed schemas to DLQs, use fencing tokens, and shed load gracefully instead of queuing until OOM.
pragmaticPrinciples.lldApplication: Validate preconditions loudly at boundaries; enforce invariants in constructors.
